transport_plan_1d — COLORTRANSPORT transport op

• Data kinds: signal × signal → transport_plan

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.transport_plan_1d(u_values, v_values) (to call the implementation directly, import colortransport; colortransport.transport_plan_1d(u_values, v_values); from the registry, opscolortransport.get("transport_plan_1d"))

Usage

The exact 1-D transport plan (north-west corner rule). Returns an (n, m) mass matrix.

Row sums are 1/n and column sums 1/m -- this is exact by construction, and it never deviates except by numerical error (pinned by a test).

Procedure: sort u (n values) and v (m values) each in ascending order, and from the smallest assign mass min(remaining u, remaining v) in turn (monotone coupling). Each sample's mass is equally 1/n and 1/m (weights are not accepted). In 1 dimension, as long as a convex function of distance is the cost, this monotone coupling is the optimal solution, so you get the same transport as wasserstein_1d as a matrix of "which sample goes where".

• u_values, v_values: flattened to 1 dimension (ravel). The lengths may differ. Empty gives MetricContractError. Finiteness is not checked (NaN is sorted to the end and silently coupled).

• Return value: float64 of shape (n, m) (transport_plan type). plan[i, j] is the mass carried from u[i] to v[j] in the original input order. At most n + m - 1 non-zero elements. If n == m, a permutation matrix / n (one-to-one correspondence).

• Complexity is an O((n + m) log) sort + an O(n + m) sweep, but the returned matrix is a dense n × m matrix, so it is not suited to samples on the scale of pixel counts (in that case histogram_match or sinkhorn).

apply_transport(plan, v) gives the destination value (centroid) of each sample on the u side, and transport_cost(plan, cost) the total cost.
